da-false-claim.evidence: lean/QOU/LiftingDescent/tm_transient_localisation.lean:50-52 — theorem tm_transient_localisation (N : ℕ) (MItotal : ℝ) (MIdiv : ℕ → ℝ) : MItotal = (Finset.range N).sum (fun i => MIdiv i)
da-false-claim.notes: As stated in Lean the equation is FALSE for arbitrary reals: with N=0 it forces MItotal = 0 for every real MItotal; with any N it equates an unconstrained MItotal to an unconstrained sum. The intended hypothesis 'h_disjoint_factorisation' the docstring (lines 43-48) claims to 'package' is NOT a binder in the signature — it was dropped. The literal proposition is a quantifier-slip counterexample (pick MItotal=1, all MIdiv=0). It only typechecks because it is discharged by `sorry` (line 57). The .md statement (a genuine norm-decomposition over disjoint divisors) is plausible; the Lean encoding is false.

da-vacuous.evidence: tm_transient_localisation.lean:50-57; .md uses MI∫ machinery with no Mathlib backing
da-vacuous.notes: The Lean carries no real content: every variable is a free real and the equation is unproved (sorry). The docstring explicitly says the prior version was a 'vacuous self-assuming projection' and this rewrite is more honest — but in dropping the factorisation hypothesis it swung from vacuous-projection to false-and-sorry'd, which is not content-bearing either. The true mathematical content (multiplicative-integral additivity over disjoint support) is entirely outside Mathlib and unformalised.

da-circular.notes: No back-fitting or smuggled calibration; the .md states a structural localisation, not a numerical target.

da-overclaim.notes: Block kind 'lemma' presents a settled result, but the entire analytic core (per-disc factorisation of the multiplicative integral) is deferred to non-existent machinery via sorry with a [manuscript] ref. A lemma whose only Lean content is an unproved (and as-encoded false) equation overclaims the 'lemma' status; honestly it is a conjectural/deferred statement.

da-hidden-dof.notes: No free numerical parameter or off-menu coefficient; structural statement.

da-non-sequitur.notes: The docstring asserts 'From it [the factorisation] the conclusion is immediate', but 'it' is not present in the theorem signature, so the conclusion does not follow from any stated hypothesis — the inference chain is broken at the type level. The .md likewise jumps from 'support contained in disjoint discs D_i' to norm-additivity over E_i without stating the additivity lemma for the multiplicative-integral norm.
